messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@cloudoptimize.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity — billing model and PO/net terms questions

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from procurement — we’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated and need to understand your billing and invoicing mechanics before we move forward with sizing:

- Do you offer both monthly invoicing and annual prepay for Dedicated reserved capacity? What discount ranges apply for annual commits versus monthly?
- How do true-ups work if usage spikes above commit? Are overages billed at on-demand rates or at a discounted overage rate?
- We need to align on PO process and Net terms (our standard is Net45 but we can be flexible for prepay). Do you accept POs and electronic signature?
- Are throughput guarantees written into the contract or only in SLAs for Dedicated? We need clarity for procurement and SRE.

Our approximate target: a pool that can sustain ~6M tokens/day steady, spikes up to ~12M tokens/day for short bursts. Happy to share telemetry. Please send any standard language or a sample invoice layout if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Cloud Ops
CloudOptimize

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below and I attached our standard Dedicated terms to this thread (Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_2025.pdf). I can follow up with a tailored quote after a quick sizing call.

High-level:
- Billing models: we support monthly invoiced reserved commits (billed at the start of each month) and annual prepay (one invoice at activation, discounted). Annual prepay typically gets the largest discount; examples below.
- Discount bands we use (examples, negotiable based on commit size and length): monthly reserved commit: 5–10% off list; 12-month prepay: 15–25% off list; multi-year: can extend beyond that with additional credits.
- True-ups/overages: we do monthly true-ups. If you exceed your committed throughput in a billing period we bill the delta at the agreed overage rate for that tier (often the committed rate or a small premium over committed rate, not full on-demand), or we’ll automatically upgrade the commit if sustained. For large spikes we can configure burst capacity pools.
- PO & terms: we accept POs and e-signatures (DocuSign). Standard enterprise terms are Net30, but for annual prepay we invoice upfront. We can consider Net45/Net60 subject to credit review for large deals; payment by ACH/wire.
- Throughput guarantees: Dedicated includes throughput SLOs tied to commit tiers and GPU-equivalent pools. Guarantees are captured in the Dedicated SLO schedule in the contract; we’ll include a clause tying response-time/throughput to the committed pool size.

Next steps: if you can share a 2-week sample of token QPS/percentile latency targets we’ll size the GPU pool and provide a line-item quote (committed GPUs, estimated monthly tokens, projected cost with both monthly and annual options).

I attached Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_2025.pdf for legal/PO review.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — billing model and PO/net terms questions

Looping you both in — Sara from CloudOptimize is asking about billing cadence and true-ups. Their numbers: steady ~6M tokens/day, spikes to ~12M. They’ve asked about PO + Net45.

My suggested commercial approach:
- Offer both monthly reserved and 12-month prepay. Give them a formal comparison:
  - Monthly reserved commit: smaller up-front, 5% discount off list, monthly invoice, monthly true-up; overages billed at committed tier rate + 10% premium.
  - 12-month prepay: invoice up-front for committed capacity, 18% discount off list, monthly reporting and no per-month invoice, true-ups reconciled quarterly (to avoid frequent billing friction).
- Tech constraints: minimum committed pool = 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (we should confirm model family), scaling increments of 4 GPUs. For their 6M steady / 12M burst, rough estimate = 12 A100-eq to hit p95 latency targets given current Redwood kernel optimizations.
- PO & terms: accept PO and DocuSign. Offer Net30 as standard; consider Net45 as a concession only if they sign 12-month prepay and provide a PO covering full year (or we require credit approval).

Question: are we comfortable offering Net45 if we take 18% off and quarterly true-up? Can we soften overage rate to committed rate (no premium) for the first 2 quarters?

Also — what flexibility do we have on minimum commit and how quickly can we add burst GPUs if they spike? Dev, can you confirm lead time and if we can guarantee hot-add within 24–48 hours for CloudOptimize?

-M

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — billing model and PO/net terms questions

Marissa — technical notes and constraints:
- Minimum: we can reasonably guarantee an 8-GPU pool as a starting point. For their workload numbers I agree ~12 A100-eq is the safer starting point to meet p95 latency targets for most prompt mixes.
- Hot-add: we can allocate additional GPUs within 6–12 hours in the same region if capacity is available; 24–48h SLA if we need to spin new machines (depends on cloud provider inventory). We can include a "burst pool" of standby instances for an additional small fee to guarantee sub-6h add.
- True-up mechanics: monthly usage tracking is trivial; billing can either bill overages at a discounted overage rate (committed rate) or bill at on-demand. From ops perspective, billing at committed rate for first two quarters makes sense as a trust-building concession, after which we revert to committed + 10% premium on transient spikes, or require them to raise the commit.
- Monitoring & evidence: we can provide token-level usage reports and a per-route breakdown for their SREs; include audit logs for billed events.

If we offer Net45 on a 12-month prepay we should require either: (a) PO for full year + 1st-month wire, or (b) credit review plus a slightly higher price (2–3% premium). Otherwise the exposure is larger than ops is comfortable with.

Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposed Dedicated commit & billing terms for CloudOptimize

Hi Sara — per our notes and internal sizing, here is a concrete proposal for CloudOptimize. I’ve attached a short SOW and our Dedicated terms for legal review (SOW_Dedicated_CloudOptimize_v1.docx; Redwood_Dedicated_Terms_2025.pdf).

Proposed commercials:
- Commit: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (24TB KV cache target), sized for ~6M steady / 12M burst tokens/day.
- Options:
  1) Monthly reserved: billed at start of each month, 7% discount off list, monthly true-up. Overages billed at committed rate + 10% premium.
  2) 12-month annual prepay: 18% discount off list, single invoice at activation, quarterly reconciliation (true-ups). We can offer Net45 on the annual prepay if CloudOptimize provides a PO covering the full year at signing OR completes a short credit check.
- Burst guarantee: offer a small standby burst pool (2 GPUs) for guaranteed <6h hot-add; otherwise hot-add within 24–48h depending on availability.
- PO & contracting: we accept PO and DocuSign e-signatures. Standard payment methods: ACH/wire. Invoice layout and contact details included in the attached terms.

Next steps:
1) Let me know which commercial option you prefer.
2) If annual prepay looks good, please send a PO for the full year and we’ll prepare DocuSign.
3) If you prefer monthly, confirm the expected steady token amount so we can finalize the monthly committed bandwidth.

If agreeable, I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff sizing call with Dev to lock in the exact GPU family and KV sizing.

Appreciate it —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
